title: NUMA affinity OOM during token-storm on continuous batching
content:
Summary:

Brief: During a traffic surge (token-storm) on 2026-02-10 we observed repeated host-level OOM events on a subset of GPU hosts running continuous batching. Symptoms looked like sudden memory accounting spike on host, containers dying with OOMKilled, but kernel logs showed host oom_reaper involvement before container rational OOM. Impact: ~12% of in-flight requests failed between 09:13-09:47 UTC, latency spikes on warm hosts, and a brief autoscaler thrash.

Why this doc: on-call notes + quick runbook draft for similar NUMA/affinity-related OOMs when batching suddenly ramps. Intended to be informal; please add corrections.

What we saw (symptoms):
- Alerts: node-memory-usage > 90% (node-exporter) and pod OOMKilled spikes.
- Hosting tier affected: p4d-large-prod pool (8 hosts). 3 hosts showed repeating OOM events.
- Metrics: continuous-batcher inflight queue length jumped 6x; per-host resident set size (RSS) rose abruptly +25GB over ~3 minutes.
- Kernel logs (dmesg): "Out of memory: Kill process 31245 (batch_worker) score 987 or sacrifice child" and repeated oom_reaper activity.
- Container logs: batch_worker stack traces showing cache resize + KV index rebuild entries immediately before OOM.
- Observed a pattern of heavy cross-NUMA remote memory accesses in perf samples.

Initial on-call timeline (UTC):
- 09:11 Alert fires: node memory high for node p4d-prod-08.
- 09:13 Pager to SRE oncall (Priya). Started ssh to node, ran top, free -h, pod list.
- 09:15 Noticed many batch_worker containers in CrashLoopBackOff. kubectl describe pod showed OOMKilled.
- 09:18 Collected kernel logs (sudo journalctl -k -n 200) and /var/log/messages. Found oom_reaper calls and pages showing "node local alloc failure" hints.
- 09:22 Scaled down continuous-batcher replica count (dynconfig) by 30% to reduce pressure. Immediate inflight queue stabilized but memory still climbing on affected hosts.
- 09:28 Evicted non-critical lower-priority pods on affected nodes (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force for two nodes) to free host memory. This allowed some batch_worker pods to restart.
- 09:35 Applied emergency kernel parameter adjust (set vm.zone_reclaim_mode=1) on affected hosts to reduce remote allocation pressure (temporary in-memory change via sysctl).
- 09:40 Memory usage plateaued and OOM frequency dropped. Traffic ramp controlled with rate-limiter tweak.
- 09:47 Incident declared mitigated; rolling restarts scheduled for the three affected hosts to apply a permanent config.

Hypothesis (root cause candidate):
A combination of:
1) A recent serving-runtime change (PR #2394) introduced a KV-cache resize path that can trigger large per-worker allocations during a rare condition (concurrent prefix eviction + cache reindex).
2) When the batcher inflight queue increased rapidly (token-storm), multiple workers concurrently hit the resize path, allocating large buffers.
3) On p4d hosts with NUMA domains, allocations became remote-heavy because the process CPU affinity was on different sockets than the bulk memory allocator preference, causing increased fragmentation and remote-node allocations.
4) Remote allocations under memory pressure tripped host-level OOM (oom_reaper) before container cgroup OOM kill thresholds behaved predictably.

Why this differs from prior KV-cache OOMs: previous incidents were correlated with persistent cache leaks or spill-to-disk events. This incident is transient, triggered by concurrency of resize path + NUMA affinity mismatch, producing very fast spikes (minutes).

Immediate fixes applied (what we did):
- Scaled down batcher replicas via dynconfig to reduce concurrent resizes.
- Drained and rebooted two hosts to clear fragmentation and reset kernel NUMA allocations.
- Toggled vm.zone_reclaim_mode=1 to prefer local caches and reduce remote allocations while we assessed.
- Short-term rate limiting on the public route to flatten token-storm surge.

Short runbook draft (for next time - quick checklist for on-call):
1) On alert that node memory > 85% and multiple pod OOMs:
   - ssh into node, run: top -o RES, ps -eo pid,ppid,cmd,%mem --sort=-%mem | head
   - check kernel logs: sudo journalctl -k -n 300 | grep -i oom
   - examine cgroup usage: cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/kubepods.slice/*/memory.usage_in_bytes (or use cgtop)
2) If multiple batch_worker pods are OOMKilled:
   - reduce continuous-batcher dynconfig replica count by 30%
   - run: kubectl get pods -o wide -l app=continuous-batcher -n infra
3) If node shows remote memory allocation failures in dmesg/perf samples:
   - set sysctl temporarily: sudo sysctl -w vm.zone_reclaim_mode=1
   - consider draining node and rebooting: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force && gcloud compute instances reset <node-instance>
4) If OOMs persist after draining other pods:
   - shift traffic away from affected region via routing policy in traffic-control console
   - escalate to infra-kernel team (pager) with collected kernel logs and perf samples
5) Capture artifacts:
   - save journalctl -k, dmesg, /proc/slabinfo, and heap profiles from batch_worker (heapdump endpoints)

Post-incident follow-ups (owners & actions):
- eng-serving-runtime: revert or patch PR #2394 hotfix to make resize path single-threaded when memory utilization is above threshold (owner: Miguel Santos, due 2026-02-16).
- eng-sre: add a node-level SLO to alert on rapid RSS growth rate (>10GB in 2m) in addition to absolute memory % (owner: Alex Chen, due 2026-02-20).
- infra-kernel: evaluate default vm.zone_reclaim_mode across p4d pools and recommend consistent setting (owner: Lina Anders, due 2026-02-22).
- product/hosting: add a traffic-shaping toggle to the public route to throttle token-level surges (owner: Priya Iyer, due 2026-03-01).

Dashboards & metrics to add:
- per-host 'RSS growth rate' chart (1m, 5m windows).
- continuous-batcher per-pod malloc/realloc counts (new exporter metric).
- perf samples dashboard showing remote vs local memory loads per process.

Notes / Gotchas observed while troubleshooting:
- container cgroup limits sometimes lagged kernel host-level kills; important to check kernel logs not just K8s pod status.
- we saw 'node local alloc failure, fallback to remote' messages in dmesg which were key to the NUMA hypothesis.
- vm.zone_reclaim_mode change helped in mitigation but is a blunt instrument; needs kernel team review.

Open questions (for follow-up):
- Can the runtime add a cheap backoff on the cache-resize path to avoid concurrent large allocations?
- How frequently do our p4d hosts experience fragmentation under normal load?
- Are there other code paths that allocate large temporary buffers during high-token loads?

Appendix: quick commands collected during oncall (paste as-is):
- sudo journalctl -k -n 500 > /tmp/kern-oom-$(date +%s).log
- kubectl get pods -n infra -l app=continuous-batcher -o wide > /tmp/batchers-$(date +%s).txt
- sudo sysctl -w vm.zone_reclaim_mode=1  # temp toggle (revert after review)
- perf record -g -p $(pidof batch_worker) -- sleep 30  # collect stack samples (needs perf installed)

If you were oncall: please add any missing details below, particularly any stack traces or heap dumps you saved. This will feed into the formal postmortem we plan to produce after the runtime hotfix is merged.
